auth.setupIntro: Choose how you will sign in. Your notes are encrypted on your devices, and you get a twelve-word phrase to keep either way. Everything you have written so far comes with you.
auth.passkeyNote: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, face or device lock. A phrase alone is like a crypto wallet: just the words, nothing to remember.
auth.phraseIntro: These twelve words are the key to your notes. If you lose every signed-in device and this phrase, your notes cannot be recovered, not even by us. Anyone who has it can read them. It is shown only now.

auth.idleText: You stepped away, so Seijaku put the key away. Your notes are still here.
auth.passkeyCannot: That passkey cannot open your notes by itself. Use your recovery phrase.

news.n1: Local-first notes that work offline, with nested pages, six note types and a block editor.
news.n2: End-to-end encrypted sync between devices: the server only holds sealed copies.

privacy.sealedLead: Your notes are sealed on your device.
privacy.sealed: Pages, titles, tags and files are encrypted before they leave it. The server stores and relays sealed data it cannot read, and names each page by a hash, not its title.
privacy.knows: That an account exists, its passkeys’ public parts, when you connect, how much sealed data you store, and which share links exist. Your recovery phrase never leaves your device; only a value derived from it is kept so it can prove it is yours.
privacy.share: A shared page is a separate sealed copy. Its key lives only in the link after the #, which browsers do not send to servers. Stopping sharing deletes the copy.
privacy.preview: When you add a link card, your server fetches that web page to read its title and picture.
privacy.device: Pages and images stay in this browser’s storage until you clear them (Settings → Data). Seijaku runs no analytics and no ads.
privacy.key: Because the server cannot read your notes, it cannot recover them either. Keep your recovery phrase somewhere safe.
